Whether the evidence supports it: No. Elo/OpenSkill ratings are stateful; the intended distinction is lack of global retroactive recomputation in the specified implementation.
Recommended revised wording: “Sequential systems usually preserve past updates; LOOPR deliberately recomputes the whole result network so later evidence can recontextualize earlier wins.”
Remaining limitation: Some Bayesian models can be smoothed or refit globally.

Current claim in the draft: “They’re gameable … [and] can’t tell the difference between a major and a local.”
Evidence offered: No direct gaming experiment in the draft.
Whether the evidence supports it: Not established. OpenSkill variants actually predict held-out matches better here.
Recommended revised wording: “A match-by-match system without event features may not encode the distinction we wanted; LOOPR attempts to do so through event influence.”
Remaining limitation: The present tournament-weighting property test is inconclusive.
Suggested main-path or collapsible place: Collapsible; remove the categorical main-path claim.

Current claim in the draft: “PageRank captures something Elo can’t: transitive relationships.”
Whether the evidence supports it: Too absolute. Both families can transmit information; LOOPR’s distinctive feature is global recontextualization over the observed graph.
Recommended revised wording: “LOOPR makes those transitive paths explicit and recomputes them globally.”
Remaining limitation: Mechanism alone does not prove better measurement.

Current claim in the draft: “The ratio is the same” / “Volume-invariant” / “It doesn’t matter how much you play.”
Evidence offered: Illustration, prior simulations, and a real-data residual test.
Whether the evidence supports it: Supports resistance, not cancellation. Standardized log-match coefficient −0.009; partial R² 0.00025 after limited controls.
Recommended revised wording: “In these data LOOPR was largely volume-resistant after accounting for record and opponent strength; it did not prove perfect volume cancellation.”
Remaining limitation: Observational controls are incomplete; opportunity and selection can still matter.
Suggested main-path or collapsible place: One sentence main path; diagnostics in a collapsible.

Current claim in the draft: “Score differences map to predicted win probabilities via Bradley–Terry.”
Whether the evidence supports it: Only after defining team aggregation and fitting a prior-only temperature; the raw scale is not automatically calibrated.
Recommended revised wording: “A single calibration parameter maps pre-event team-score differences to win probabilities.”
Remaining limitation: Reliability still departs from the diagonal in some bins.

Current claim in the draft: Tournament-strength weighting prevents farming weaker events.
Evidence offered: Intended tick-tock mechanism; observed event-removal check.
Whether the evidence supports it: Not demonstrated. The signed contribution pattern does not cleanly show weak-event damping.
Recommended revised wording: “Tournament influence is designed to reduce weak-event leverage; this audit did not establish complete or even clean monotonic resistance.”
Remaining limitation: Event strength is model-derived and event categories are not randomized.
Suggested main-path or collapsible place: Technical collapsible; no main-path success claim.

Current claim in the draft: Exposure teleportation prevents sparse players from swinging wildly.
Evidence offered: 24 one-match perturbations with and without smoothing.
Whether the evidence supports it: Not demonstrated by this test; smoothed and unsmoothed movement were nearly identical.
Recommended revised wording: “Exposure teleportation is intended as regularization, but this small perturbation test did not show a material stability gain.”
Remaining limitation: Only six sampled players per exposure band; rank movement is noisy.

Current claim in the draft: The 180-day half-life is the appropriate setting.
Whether the evidence supports it: Supports a reasonable tradeoff, not a unique optimum. Ninety days predicts slightly better (0.511 vs 0.513 log loss).
Recommended revised wording: “Several settings performed similarly. We retained 180 days as an explainable recency–continuity choice, not an empirically unique optimum.”
Remaining limitation: No formal utility function combines responsiveness and continuity.
Suggested main-path or collapsible place: Short main-path note; full sweep collapsible.

Whether the evidence supports it: Partly. Revised accuracy is 0.748; calibration is monotone but imperfect. Log loss should be primary.
Recommended revised wording: “LOOPR’s held-out log loss was 0.513, versus 0.578 for recent win rate and 0.693 for chance; its reliability curve was directionally sensible but not perfect.”
Remaining limitation: Accuracy is threshold-dependent and does not measure probability quality.
Suggested main-path or collapsible place: Main prediction table and reliability figure.

Current claim in the draft: LOOPR and OpenSkill are “essentially the same” / “by all our metrics.”
Whether the evidence supports it: No. All three stronger identity-only baselines have clearly lower paired held-out log loss than LOOPR.
Recommended revised wording: “The systems share signal but differ materially in predictive performance and in some subgroup behavior.”
Remaining limitation: No baseline is a ground truth for latent skill.

Evidence offered: No evidence needed for the actual comparison; the label is rhetorical.
Whether the evidence supports it: Avoid. It neither strengthens the design nor makes OpenSkill a reference truth.
Recommended revised wording: “We included OpenSkill μ and ordinal as existing Bayesian baselines.”

Evidence offered: Figure and draft assertion; no recoverable protocol or saved row.
Whether the evidence supports it: No. The value is unreproduced. Revised institutional macro AUC is 0.777 (95% CI 0.719–0.831).
Recommended revised wording: “Averaged equally across the three tier-specific comparisons, the passer-above-failer probability was 77.7%.”
Remaining limitation: Only 310 of 468 candidates met the predeclared 90-day activity definition.

Current claim in the draft: LOOPR is “excellent at identifying what players classify as skill.”
Whether the evidence supports it: Too broad. Like-for-like tier/status AUC is 0.615, and its advantage over activity alone is unresolved.
Recommended revised wording: “LOOPR was concordant with this consequential vote, especially at the institutional tier level; agreement weakened under like-for-like comparison.”
Remaining limitation: One vote snapshot may encode reputation, access, visibility, and current rules.

Current claim in the draft: Agreement is “mutual validation” proving both capture “something real about player skill.”
Whether the evidence supports it: Convergent evidence, not proof. The shuffle control shows outcome direction adds information; subjectivity is not a defect.
Recommended revised wording: “The vote supplies convergent evidence from a differently aggregated community judgment.”
Remaining limitation: The sources are not fully independent because both arise from the same competitive community.

Current claim in the draft: Disagreeing after validation is a “tough position.”
Whether the evidence supports it: No. Aggregate evidence does not adjudicate every exact pair or make criticism illegitimate.
Recommended revised wording: Remove. Add: “A high AUC supports broad ordering, not every neighboring rank.”
Remaining limitation: Individual reversals can be both socially meaningful and statistically unresolved.
Suggested main-path or collapsible place: Main limitation; sets up Part II.

Current claim in the draft: LOOPR “extracts skill” / contains a “real skill signal.”
Whether the evidence supports it: Only with a bounded construct. No objective player-skill vector is observed.
Recommended revised wording: “LOOPR contains substantial outcome-derived information about demonstrated organized-play success.”
Remaining limitation: It can also reflect access, teammate quality, opportunity, and network position.
Suggested main-path or collapsible place: Construct definition at the start and conclusion.

Whether the evidence supports it: Too vague. Some tests support LOOPR; stronger baselines predict better, smoothing/weighting are unresolved, and novel-lineup transfer is weak.
Recommended revised wording: Name the supported property each time: predictive information, vote concordance, stability, or robustness.
Remaining limitation: No single metric validates exact rank accuracy.

Current claim in the draft: Predictive and vote evidence establish leaderboard legitimacy.
Evidence offered: Implicit bridge in the validation and skeptic sections.
Whether the evidence supports it: No. Measurement quality and legitimacy are different levels of claim.
Recommended revised wording: “Part I supports an outcome-derived skill-o-meter. Whether named exact ranks should govern public status is Part II’s question.”
Remaining limitation: Publication creates social and institutional effects not measured here.
